next_mission_recommendation.mission_description: Now that StoryForge has robust error logging and reporting, the next step is to make the Gemini integration self-healing. Build an automatic retry system that uses the error categories from logging_system.py to make intelligent retry decisions: retry with exponential backoff for rate limits and timeouts, prompt reformulation for safety filter blocks, graceful fallback to Claude when Gemini auth fails, and automatic API key validation on startup. Add a provider health dashboard showing success/failure rates per provider, average latency, and cost tracking. Implement circuit-breaker pattern so that repeated failures on one provider automatically route to the backup provider without user intervention.
next_mission_recommendation.rationale: The logging system built in this mission provides the error categorization foundation needed for intelligent auto-recovery. Cycle 1: retry logic with exponential backoff and circuit breaker. Cycle 2: provider fallback routing and health monitoring. Cycle 3: startup validation, provider health dashboard, and end-to-end testing under failure conditions. This directly builds on the 10 error categories and retryability detection already implemented.

final_report.summary: Successfully diagnosed and fixed StoryForge's opaque error reporting system. The original problem was that users saw only 'Failed at stage: RESEARCH' with no explanation of WHY. Built a comprehensive structured logging system (sf_engine/logging_system.py) with 10 error categories, dual output (text + JSON), and user-friendly message generation. Fully integrated the logger into the orchestrator, database, routes, and WebSocket broadcast pipeline so that detailed, actionable error messages now flow end-to-end from the LLM provider all the way to the browser UI. Added database migration for an error_message column, a new /api/projects/{id}/logs endpoint for debugging, and 8 dedicated tests validating the entire error flow. All 66 tests pass. The fix is backward-compatible, provider-agnostic (works with Gemini, Claude, and future providers), and production-ready.

All 66 tests passing with zero breaking changes to existing functionality
challenges_overcome: Tracing the full error flow from Gemini API through multiple layers (provider -> orchestrator -> state_manager -> database -> routes -> WebSocket -> UI) to identify where error details were being dropped
Designing a logging system that serves two audiences: end users (need simple actionable messages) and developers (need full stack traces and context)
Adding database schema changes (error_message column) with backward-compatible migration for existing projects
Ensuring the logging system is provider-agnostic so it works with Claude, Gemini, and any future LLM providers
lessons_learned: Error messages should be designed for TWO audiences from the start: users need actionable guidance, developers need technical details - serve both with structured logging
When debugging 'why does X fail', trace the FULL data flow end-to-end rather than fixing one layer - the error detail was available at the provider but lost in transit through multiple layers
Database schema changes for error tracking should be planned early - retrofitting error_message columns requires migration logic
Categorizing errors (auth, timeout, rate limit, safety filter) enables both better user messages AND automated retry decisions
JSONL format for structured error logs enables post-hoc analysis and pattern detection across sessions
